sentences.text:

 Dated this the 4th day of June, 2024  JUDGMENT Petitioner has approached this Court seeking a direction to the 3rd respondent to consider Ext.P9 and also for a direction to the 4th respondent to consider and pass orders on Exts.P7 and P8 request submitted by the petitioner.
2.

It is averred that the petitioner is the absolute owner in possession of the property having an extent of 2.263 Cents (0.92 Ares) situated in Survey No.39/1-12 in Poonithura Village and two storied building situated therein having Door Nos.35/1405-A, and 35/1405-B (New Nos.44/382 and 44/383) of the Corporation of Cochin, which was purchased by the mother of the petitioner as per Ext.P1 sale deed.

Petitioner's mother applied for a building permit before the local authority and constructed a two storied building in the above said property and as per Ext.P5 partition deed the property was allotted in favour of the petitioner.

Thereafter, petitioner effected mutation of the property and has been paying tax in respect of the property, as evident from Ext.P6.
3.
The grievance raised by the petitioner is that attempt is being made to take over the land of the petitioner for the extension of Kochi Metro Rail to Kakkanad.

The specific case of the petitioner is that petitioner has not surrendered any portion of the land and if the authorities require the property of the petitioner, the same can only be after following the procedure prescribed under the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 and after giving due compensation.

entities.text: Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: When the petitioner approached the 3rd respondent it was intimated that the petitioner has already relinquished a portion of the land in favour of the 4th respondent and that such information has been provided to the 3rd respondent by the 4th respondent.
Petitioner submits that he has not relinquished his right over any piece of land covered by Exts.P1 and P5.
Thereupon, petitioner has preferred Ext.P7 request before the GCDA, the 4th respondent herein for providing certain details including the details of the property surrendered by the petitioner.
Petitioner has also approached the 3rd respondent by filing Ext.P9 wherein also he has sought for certain document regarding free surrender of land in favour of GCDA.
Petitioner seeks for a direction to respondents 3 and 4 to dispose of Exts.P7 and P9 pending before the said authorities.

4. After hearing the learned counsel for the petitioner, the learned Government Pleader as well as the learned Standing Counsel for the 3rd respondent, the above writ petition is disposed of with a direction to the 3rd respondent to consider and pass orders on Ext.P9 and also directing the 4th respondent to consider and pass orders on Exts.P7 and P8 request submitted by the petitioner and pass final orders on the same at the earliest, at any rate, within an outer limit of 3 weeks from the Dinu Philip P vs The State Of Kerala on 4 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/16306594/
